      Search — find stories by meaning

      Semantic search

      ranked by meaning, not keywords · runs in your browser

        Runs entirely in your browser via transformers.js — your query is embedded with the same BGE family used to build the map and matched against the articles by cosine similarity. The first search downloads a small model (~30 MB) from a CDN and caches it; after that it works offline. The rest of the page needs no network at all.

        Discovered topics — clusters found by meaning

        Topic map & anomalies

        the clusters above, laid out and listed

        Built from scratch from the article embeddings (BGE), not the keyword buckets. HDBSCAN groups the stories into data-driven clusters, each named by the key phrase whose meaning sits closest to the cluster (embedding similarity × distinctiveness). Topics are tracked across days, so a topic keeps the same name and colour build to build. Embeds each story's headline + body; off-topic stories fall out as Other.

        Topic river — what's rising, fading, appearing

        Each band is a discovered topic; thickness = articles that period. Select topics with the chips, pick the grain, drag the range handles to zoom, and click a band to read its articles. Bands swell, shrink, appear and vanish; hover one for its count.

        grain

        Escalation tone — is coverage heating up? de-escalationbaselineescalation

        Each story scored on an escalation vs de-escalation axis (cosine to anchor phrases in the same embedding space), relative to this feed's own baseline. Rows = discovered topics by week; the top All coverage row is the overall trend. Colour = mean tone; deeper red = more escalatory. Number = articles that week — click any number to list those articles.

          Anomalies — the most isolated stories

            Sources: ERR (Estonia), LRT (Lithuania), LSM (Latvia), English editions.
            Method: headlines filtered to defence/geopolitics themes, full article bodies fetched. Themes are hand-authored keyword buckets, not clusters: an article is tagged with every bucket its words hit (headline weighted) and coloured by the strongest — so it can appear under more than one theme. A separate semantic layer embeds each story with BGE sentence-embeddings and discovers topics by clustering them (BERTopic / HDBSCAN); the search box matches your query by meaning, embedding it in your browser with transformers.js. Named entities come from spaCy. The most frequent terms are tallied across the article titles: with common English stopwords and the Baltic countries' own names and capitals removed, so only the distinctive words surface; word variants (russia/russian, drone/drones) count as one.
